Corebeam Telecom -- Device Installment Plan Terms, Section 6

6.1 Devices financed via 24-month installment plans may be paid off early at any time
with no prepayment penalty.
6.2 Trade-in credit toward a new device requires the old device's installment balance to
be paid off first. Trade-in value exceeding the remaining balance is issued as bill
credit spread evenly over the following 3 months, not as a lump sum or cash.
6.3 Devices reported lost or stolen are not eligible for trade-in credit, and the
remaining installment balance becomes immediately due in full.
6.4 A device with any unresolved insurance claim is not eligible for trade-in until the
claim is closed.

Case file -- Elif Sahin has $240 remaining on her device installment plan ($20/month, 12
months left). She trades it in for a new phone; the assessed trade-in value is $300. No
insurance claims are open on the device, and it has not been reported lost or stolen.

questions.instruction: How is Elif's $60 excess trade-in value credited to her?

candidates.description: As a $60 lump-sum cash payment
As a single $60 bill credit
As three monthly bill credits of $20 each
Applied directly to the new device's price

questions.notes: $300 trade-in minus $240 balance = $60 excess, spread evenly over 3 months per 6.2: $20/month.

questions.instruction: Which of the following are true about Elif's trade-in?

candidates.description: Her remaining balance is paid off via the trade-in value
The excess value is paid out as cash
The excess value is credited over 3 months
Her device was reported lost or stolen
Her device is eligible for trade-in

questions.notes: $300 covers her $240 balance with $60 excess credited over 3 months; she has no lost/stolen report or open claim, so she's eligible.

PulseFit Family Membership Billing, Section 8

8.1 Family memberships bill monthly in advance; adding a family member mid-cycle is
prorated based on days remaining in the billing cycle (daily rate = monthly fee / 30,
regardless of the actual number of days in that calendar month).
8.2 Removing a family member mid-cycle takes effect at the START of the next billing
cycle; no partial-month refund is given for the current cycle.
8.3 The primary account holder is always billed the full monthly rate; only additional
members' fees are prorated when added.
8.4 A family membership requires a minimum of 2 people; removing a member that would drop
the account below 2 automatically converts the account to an Individual membership at the
next cycle.

Case file -- The Kim family plan: primary holder + 1 additional member (2 people total).
Additional-member fee is $30/month. On day 10 of a 30-day billing cycle, they add a
second additional member (3 people total).

questions.instruction: How much is the Kim family charged for adding the new member mid-cycle?
questions.notes: 20 days remain in the 30-day cycle after day 10; daily rate $30/30=$1; 20 x $1 = $20.

questions.instruction: Which of the following are true about the Kim family's billing?

candidates.description: The new member's fee is prorated
The primary holder's fee is prorated
The addition takes effect in the current cycle
The account still qualifies as a family membership
The account converts to an Individual membership

questions.notes: The new member is prorated and added immediately (unlike removals); the primary is never prorated; 3 people is still above the 2-person minimum.

Brightwater University -- Dining Services Meal Plan Refund Policy, Section 9

9.1 Withdrawing within the first 2 weeks of the semester: 100% refund of unused balance.
9.2 Withdrawing between week 3 and week 8: 50% refund of unused balance.
9.3 Withdrawing after week 8: no refund.
9.4 Medical withdrawal, verified by Student Health Services, at any point in the
semester: 100% refund of unused balance regardless of timing, overriding 9.1-9.3.
9.5 "Unused balance" is the remaining dollar amount on the meal plan card at the time of
withdrawal, not a prorated calculation based on time remaining.

Case file -- Owen Patel withdrew from his meal plan in week 5 of the semester, for
non-medical reasons, with $420 remaining on his card (out of an original $800 balance).

questions.instruction: How much refund is Owen entitled to?
questions.notes: Week 5 falls in the week 3-8 bracket: 50% of the $420 UNUSED balance = $210, not 50% of the original $800.

questions.instruction: Which of the following are true about Owen's refund?

candidates.description: Qualifies for a 100% refund
Qualifies for a 50% refund
The refund is based on the unused balance, not the original balance
The medical withdrawal override applies
The refund amount is $210

questions.notes: Week 5 gets the 50% tier, calculated on the $420 unused balance, yielding $210; not 100%, and no medical override applies.

DriveEasy Rentals -- Ancillary Equipment Fees, Section 12

12.1 GPS unit rental: $8/day, capped at $40 total per rental regardless of length.
12.2 Toll transponder: $4/day usage fee plus actual tolls incurred; the $4/day fee is
capped at $60 total per rental, but actual toll charges are never capped.
12.3 Keeping equipment past the return date without notifying DriveEasy triggers a $75
lost-equipment fee per item, which replaces (not adds to) the daily rental fee for the
overdue period.
12.4 Renting both a GPS and a transponder together for 10+ days gets a 10% discount on
the combined equipment fees only (not tolls, not the base rental).

Case file -- Jasmine Cole rented both a GPS and a toll transponder for a 12-day rental
and incurred $45 in actual tolls. Both items were returned on time.

questions.instruction: What is Jasmine's GPS fee for the 12-day rental, before any multi-item discount?
questions.notes: $8/day x 12 days = $96, but capped at $40 total per rental (12.1).

questions.instruction: Which of the following are true about Jasmine's equipment charges?

candidates.description: The GPS fee hit its cap
The transponder daily fee hit its cap
She qualifies for the 10% multi-item discount
Her actual tolls are discounted
Her actual tolls are capped

questions.notes: GPS hits its $40 cap; the transponder's $48 daily-fee total is under its $60 cap; renting both for 12 days (>=10) qualifies for the discount, which never applies to tolls.

BazaarHub Marketplace -- Seller-Initiated Cancellation Policy, Section 10

10.1 If a seller cancels a confirmed order for any reason, the buyer receives an
automatic full refund within 3 business days, plus a $10 platform credit as compensation,
regardless of order size.
10.2 If the cancellation reason is a pricing error, the seller MAY alternatively offer the
buyer the item at the corrected price instead of cancelling outright; the buyer may
accept or decline, and if declined (or if the seller doesn't offer it at all), 10.1
applies as normal.
10.3 Sellers who cancel more than 5% of their orders in a rolling 30-day period lose Top
Rated badge eligibility for 90 days, regardless of cancellation reason.
10.4 The $10 compensation credit in 10.1 does not apply if the buyer requested the
cancellation themselves.

Case file -- Seller Tundra Outfitters cancelled buyer Wren Castillo's $85 order due to a
pricing error (the item was mistakenly listed at $85 instead of the intended $150).
Tundra did not offer Wren the item at the corrected price; they simply cancelled and
issued a refund.

questions.instruction: What compensation is Wren entitled to, beyond her $85 refund?

candidates.description: A $10 platform credit
A $15 platform credit
An additional $85 (double refund)

questions.notes: 10.2's corrected-price offer is optional for the seller; since Tundra simply cancelled, 10.1's standard $10 compensation credit applies.

questions.instruction: Which of the following are true about this cancellation?

candidates.description: Wren gets a full refund
Wren gets a $10 platform credit
Tundra was required to offer the item at the corrected price
The cancellation was buyer-initiated
The seller cancelled due to a pricing error

questions.notes: Wren gets her refund plus the $10 credit since Tundra (not Wren) cancelled; offering the corrected price was optional, not required.

City of Rivendale -- Short-Term Rental Ordinance, Section 30

30.1 Short-term rental (STR) permits are issued only for the owner's PRIMARY residence
(owner lives there 9+ months/year); non-owner-occupied investment properties are
categorically ineligible.
30.2 Permitted STRs may be rented whole-home, while the owner is away, for a maximum of
120 days per calendar year; exceeding 120 days requires reclassification as a full Bed &
Breakfast.
30.3 Renting a room while the owner is present (a "hosted" rental) is not subject to the
120-day cap at all; only whole-home rentals while the owner is away are capped.
30.4 A single violation of the 120-day cap results in a warning; a second violation within
24 months results in permit revocation for 2 years.

Case file -- Lucia Fernandez rents her whole home to STR guests while she is away; it is
her primary residence (she lives there 10 months/year). This calendar year she rented the
whole home while away for 135 days total. She has no prior cap violations.

questions.instruction: What is the consequence of Lucia's 135 days of whole-home rentals this year?

candidates.description: No consequence; she is within the cap
A warning, as a first violation
Immediate permit revocation
Automatic B&B reclassification with no warning

questions.notes: 135 days exceeds the 120-day cap on whole-home-while-away rentals; with no prior violations, 30.4 issues a warning for this first offense.

questions.instruction: Which of the following are true about Lucia's STR situation?

candidates.description: She exceeds the 120-day cap
Her home qualifies as her primary residence
Her rentals qualify as hosted and are exempt from the cap
The first-violation warning applies to her
Her permit is automatically revoked

questions.notes: She exceeds the cap and qualifies as primary residence, triggering a first-violation warning; her rentals are whole-home-while-away, not hosted, and revocation only follows a second violation.

Aegis Smart Appliance Warranty Addendum, Section 9

9.1 Hardware components are covered under the standard hardware warranty tier terms.
9.2 Software/connectivity features (WiFi module, companion app) are covered for 1 year
from purchase ONLY, regardless of which hardware tier was purchased; this cannot be
extended by Extended or Premium tier purchases -- software coverage is a flat 1 year
across all tiers.
9.3 If a software issue causes physical hardware damage, the hardware damage IS covered
under the applicable hardware warranty tier, even though the root cause was software.
9.4 Software coverage does not include compatibility with future app updates released
after the 1-year window; features that stop working due to a later app update are not
covered.

Case file -- Wendy Zhou has a Premium-tier (5-year hardware) smart refrigerator warranty,
purchased 2 years ago. Her WiFi connectivity module stopped syncing with the app 2 years
in; a recent app update appears to have broken compatibility with her fridge's older
firmware. No physical hardware damage occurred.

questions.instruction: Is Wendy's WiFi connectivity issue covered under her warranty?

candidates.description: Covered under her Premium hardware tier
Covered because it's within the 1-year software window
Not covered; the software coverage window has lapsed
Not covered; she has no active warranty of any kind

questions.notes: Software/connectivity coverage is a flat 1 year regardless of tier (9.2); at year 2 it has lapsed, and the app-update cause is separately excluded by 9.4.

questions.instruction: Which of the following are true about Wendy's coverage?

candidates.description: She has a Premium hardware tier
Her software coverage is still active
The issue was caused by an app update after year 1
Premium extends her software coverage window
The issue is physical hardware damage

questions.notes: She has Premium hardware coverage and the cause is a post-year-1 app update; software coverage has lapsed and Premium never extends it; no hardware damage occurred.

VoyageGuard Travel Insurance Certificate, Section 18 (Family/Group Policies)

18.1 A Family Policy covers up to 5 named travelers under one policy; each named traveler
has their own individual per-category benefit limits (e.g., each gets their own $10,000
trip cancellation maximum) -- limits are not pooled across family members.
18.2 Exception: the Baggage Loss benefit IS pooled for family policies: a single combined
$3,000 maximum applies across ALL family members combined, not per person.
18.3 A traveler added to a Family Policy after the policy's original purchase date is not
covered for any pre-existing conditions, even if other family members qualify for the
pre-existing condition waiver.
18.4 Cancelling a trip for one family member's covered reason allows ALL family members
on the policy to claim trip cancellation, since the trip itself is disrupted for the
group.

Case file -- The Whitfield family (4 members) holds a Family Policy. One member's
checked bag was lost ($1,800 in losses); a different member's bag was also lost ($1,500
in losses) on the same trip. Combined baggage loss claims: $3,300.

questions.instruction: How much can the Whitfield family recover in total for both lost bags?
questions.notes: 18.2 pools Baggage Loss at a combined $3,000 family maximum; even though actual losses total $3,300, recovery is capped at $3,000.

questions.instruction: Which of the following are true about the Whitfields' Family Policy?

candidates.description: The Baggage Loss benefit is pooled across the family
Trip cancellation limits are pooled across the family
The family can recover the full $3,300
Each member has their own $10,000 trip cancellation limit
The policy covers up to 5 named travelers

questions.notes: Baggage loss is pooled (capping recovery below $3,300) while trip cancellation limits remain per-person; the policy's max is 5 travelers.

Meridian Corp Employee Handbook, Section 23 (Commuter Benefits)

23.1 Employees may elect up to $315/month pre-tax for transit and up to $315/month
pre-tax for parking (separate caps; both can be used simultaneously up to $630/month
combined).
23.2 Unused transit/parking funds roll over month to month indefinitely while employed;
there is no "use it or lose it" within a plan year.
23.3 Upon termination of employment (voluntary or involuntary), any unused commuter
balance is forfeited; it cannot be cashed out or refunded under any circumstance.
23.4 Employees may change their monthly election amount at any time, effective the
following month, not retroactively.

Case file -- Nora Lindqvist elects $200/month transit + $100/month parking = $300/month
combined. She has accumulated $450 in unused rolled-over transit funds after 3 years of
under-spending. She resigns, with her last day being the end of the month.

questions.instruction: What happens to Nora's $450 unused commuter balance when she resigns?

candidates.description: Paid out to her in cash
Rolled over to her new employer's plan
Forfeited, with no cash-out
Converted into extra PTO

questions.notes: 23.3: any unused commuter balance is forfeited upon termination, with no cash-out under any circumstance.

questions.instruction: Which of the following are true about Nora's commuter benefit situation?

candidates.description: Her combined election exceeds the $630 cap
Her unused funds are forfeited at termination
Her unused funds could roll over indefinitely while she remained employed
She can cash out her balance upon resignation
Her transit election exceeds the $315 cap

questions.notes: Her $300 combined election is well under the $630 cap and her $200 transit election is under $315; her balance rolled over while employed but is forfeited (no cash-out) now that she's resigning.
